posts.title: Newark's Lincoln Park Music Festival Returns for Another Summer of House, Hip-Hop, Gospel & More
posts.author: WAJ Editorial
posts.summary: The Lincoln Park Music Festival — Newark's largest free outdoor multi-genre music festival — returns to historic Lincoln Park this summer with two weeks of House, Hip-Hop, R&B, Gospel, and more.
posts.content:
Every summer, historic Lincoln Park in Newark becomes something bigger than a festival. It becomes a gathering place — for House heads and gospel lovers, for hip-hop fans and jazz devotees, for families and communities who come together around what they share: a love of music, a pride in Newark, and a connection to something that's been building here for over twenty years.

The Lincoln Park Music Festival (LPMF) is back for another year, and it remains one of the largest free outdoor music festivals of its kind in the entire region. With an average annual attendance that reaches well into the tens of thousands, LPMF has grown from its origins as a three-day event in 2005 into a two-weekend institution that draws visitors from across New Jersey and the Northeast.

The festival features an eclectic multi-genre lineup spanning House Music, Hip-Hop, R&B, Gospel, Jazz, and more — showcasing Grammy Award-winning acts alongside the most exciting emerging talent in New Jersey. Alongside the performances, the festival includes programming in technology, digital media, and music education, staying true to its roots as more than a concert — it's a cultural experience.

The festival is presented by the Lincoln Park Coast Cultural District (LPCCD) and organized by Newark Arts through the Festivals United Newark platform. LPCCD produces community events and arts programming year-round, but this annual festival is its signature moment — a celebration of Newark's identity as a city where music is woven into the fabric of everyday life.

Lincoln Park's House Music Day remains the festival's most anticipated single event — an electric, hours-long celebration of the genre that has always called Newark home. It's a day where the dance floor extends across a park, where generations find each other in the music, and where Newark's connection to the global House Music movement gets its proper recognition.

The festival is free and open to the public. Accessible via mass transit, with shuttle services typically available from various parts of the city to the Arts & Education District.

For the most current lineup, schedule, and ticketed event information, visit newarkarts.org or follow @lincolnparkmusicfestival on Instagram.

posts.title: NJ Pastor Walks 40 Miles from Underground Railroad Site to Trenton, Demands Passage of Reparations Bills
posts.author: WAJ Editorial
posts.summary: Rev. Dr. Robert Turner completed a 40-mile walk from Lawnside's Peter Mott House to the New Jersey State Capitol, spotlighting a petition demanding passage of two historic reparations bills — as New Jersey remains the last northern state to abolish slavery.
posts.content:
Rev. Dr. Robert Turner, pastor of Empowerment Temple AME Church and a Commissioner with the National African American Reparations Commission (NAARC), completed a 40-mile walk on July 14, 2026, from the Peter Mott House — a documented Underground Railroad site in Lawnside, NJ — to the New Jersey State Capitol in Trenton.

The walk, the 46th in his ongoing "40 Miles for 40 Acres" campaign, drew attention to an active petition that calls for the passage of two bills now before the New Jersey Legislature. The petition specifically cites New Jersey's status as the last northern state to abolish slavery.

The walk was preceded by a community talk on the evening of Monday, July 13, at the historic Burlington Quaker Meeting House & Center for Conference in Burlington, NJ — a site where Friends have gathered for over 300 years. Rev. Turner discussed his book, Creating a Culture of Repair, and the history behind Walk #46.

The petition points to stark disparities that define New Jersey's racial wealth landscape: a $662,500 gap in median household wealth between white families and Black and Latino families; a homeownership gap of 76.6% white versus 41.3% Black that has barely moved in a decade; and the nation's worst Black-white incarceration disparity — with Black residents incarcerated at 12.5 times the rate of white residents, despite comprising only 15% of the state's population.

The petition calls on the Legislature to pass two specific bills: A1665, which would establish a New Jersey Reparations Task Force, and A5253, the Truth, Reconciliation, and Repair Act of New Jersey — a bill that moves beyond study into a framework of acknowledgment, accountability, and redress.

Reparations task force legislation has been introduced and failed in New Jersey five times — in 2005, 2019, 2022, 2024, and now again as A1665. Despite that, more than fifteen municipalities including Newark, Orange, and Essex County have already passed local resolutions in support.

The walk was organized in solidarity with a broad coalition including the New Jersey Institute for Social Justice, Salvation and Social Justice, the Religious Society of Friends (Quakers) of New Jersey, the New Jersey Reparations Council, NJ Faith Allies — Say The Word, Faith in New Jersey, the New Jersey Coalition of Religious Leaders, UU FaithAction NJ, and the African Methodist Episcopal Church.

"Acknowledgment without accountability is incomplete," said Rev. Turner. "The path to genuine repair runs through Trenton."

For more information or to sign the petition, contact Rev. Dr. Robert Turner at RobertTurner15@Hotmail.com or follow @Revdrrobertturner on Instagram.

posts.title: Grammy-Winners Erica Campbell and Jonathan McReynolds Headline Free Middlesex County Gospel Music Festival July 25
posts.author: WAJ Editorial
posts.summary: Middlesex County's third annual Gospel Music Festival brings Grammy Award-winning artists Erica Campbell and Jonathan McReynolds to New Brunswick for a free outdoor concert on July 25, 2026 — with new amenities, food vendors, and transit options for attendees.
posts.content:
Middlesex County is bringing its third annual Gospel Music Festival back to New Brunswick on Saturday, July 25, 2026, from 3:30 PM to 7:30 PM at 2 Livingston Avenue — and this year's lineup is its most star-studded yet.

The free outdoor concert, part of the County's FolkLIVE community event series, will be headlined by Grammy Award-winning performers Erica Campbell and Jonathan McReynolds, joined by Billboard chart-topping gospel group The Group Fire from Newark. Local artists rounding out the lineup include Tangie Cobb, Valarie Adams, Bishop George C. Searight & Royal Priesthood, Myles Cherrette, and DJ RunTheFade. The event will be emceed by Toya Beasley, host of 94.7 The Block, and nationally recognized arts administrator Deonté Griffin-Quick.

New additions to this year's festival make the experience more accessible. The New Brunswick Performing Arts Center (NBPAC), adjacent to the festival grounds, will serve as a cooling center and offer a live streaming option. The Heldrich Hotel and Conference Center is offering a promotional rate of $119 per night for concertgoers through group code 665687, valid until July 3, 2026.

Food and beverage vendors will be on-site, including Delta's Patty Wagon, McGriff's Fish and Chips, Just Pies by Lisa, Devvon's Lemonade, and Jamaica Taste. Free and paid parking will be available, and Middlesex County RIDE shuttles will transport guests between parking areas and the event. The festival is also accessible via NJ TRANSIT Northeast Corridor Line and Amtrak at New Brunswick station.

The County encourages attendees to bring their own lawn chairs, sun protection, and cooling accessories.

"In Middlesex County, we know that access to free and affordable arts and culture can transform a community," said Commissioner Director Ronald G. Rios. "Events like the annual Gospel Music Festival transcend race and religion — it's a cultural event that unites and inspires people from all backgrounds."

"FolkLIVE Gospel Music Festival is an event dear to my heart," added Commissioner Chanelle Scott McCullum. "People will travel miles for this event, and I have no doubt this year's stellar lineup will draw crowds from all over the Northeast. It's going to be unforgettable!"

The Festival has previously featured Hezekiah Walker, Jekalyn Carr, Fred Hammond, Kierra Sheard-Kelly, and local talents including The Jenkin Brothers, Lenore Davis, David Cross, and Tawanda Muslim.

For full event details, visit middlesexcountyculture.com.

posts.title: WAJ Magazine Has a Brand New Home
posts.author: WAJ Editorial
posts.summary: After 10+ years and 42 issues, WAJ Magazine is now fully independent with its own home at wajmagazine.com — built for the creatives, entrepreneurs, and community voices we've always existed to amplify.
posts.content:
For over a decade, WAJ Magazine has told the stories of the people shaping culture in New Jersey and beyond — the artists, the entrepreneurs, the athletes, and the community leaders who don't always get the spotlight they deserve.

Today, we're proud to launch our own independent home at wajmagazine.com. Every issue we've ever published, all 42 of them, is now available right here — both as digital downloads and physical print copies you can hold in your hands.

This is more than a new website. It's a new chapter. WAJ Magazine is growing into a full media brand with its own blog, its own features program, and its own voice — while staying true to where we started: two friends from Bergen County who believed the people doing the real work in our community deserved a real platform.

Want to be featured? Have a story to tell? We're opening submissions to our community. Submit your story and our editorial team will take it from there.

Thank you for a decade of support. Here's to the next one.

posts.title: Honey Bxby Covers Issue 042 — New Jersey's Own
posts.author: WAJ Editorial
posts.summary: Honey Bxby takes the cover of WAJ Magazine Issue 042, bringing her unmistakable presence and New Jersey roots to the forefront of our latest issue.
posts.content:
There's a reason Honey Bxby's name keeps coming up in conversations about New Jersey's rising creative scene. Her presence is magnetic, her work is unapologetically her own, and Issue 042 of WAJ Magazine captures exactly that.

Inside this issue, we sit down with Honey Bxby to talk about her journey, the moments that shaped her, and what it means to represent New Jersey on her own terms. We also feature an exclusive interview with Tripp Fontane of "Tripp After Dark," diving into the creative culture that connects this community together.

Issue 042 is available now in both digital and print. Grab your copy and see why New Jersey keeps producing some of the most compelling voices in culture today.

posts.title: We're Opening Submissions — Get Featured in WAJ Magazine
posts.author: WAJ Editorial
posts.summary: WAJ Magazine has officially opened community submissions for our Features program. Merit-based selection, no payment required — just real stories from real people.
posts.content:
Since 2014, WAJ Magazine has been built on one core belief: every community has voices worth amplifying, and most of them never get asked to share their story. We're changing that in a bigger way.

We've officially opened our Features submission program to the public. Whether you're a musician, an entrepreneur, an athlete, a community organizer, or someone doing something meaningful that the world should know about — we want to hear from you.

Our selection process is entirely merit-based. There is no payment required to submit, and no payment required to be featured. Our editorial team reads every single submission and selects features based on your story, your impact, and your connection to the culture and community we cover.

Head to our Features page to submit your story. If selected, our team will reach out within 30 days to take things further.

This is your platform. Use it.
